title: How do you backtest your AI decision making system?
author: Ok-Draft2744
selftext:
I am looking to backtest and improve my own AI decision making system. So far I've been forward-testing it with real time data or snapshots, but I'd like something to give me faster feedback. 

Here is what I am thinking, create a set of daily snapshots of the data I need, some I will need to capture live if no historical version is available (say news or another type of sentiment which is harder to retrieve historically at a time point). Then give that data to an agent to make a trading decision, likely one of the subscriptions I have (API calls fees are expensive), then record that as a baseline. Improve the prompt, run again, classic backtesting. 

The more advanced version includes Fable managing the improvement. Now I am wary of this step as the chances of over-fitting and applying forward knowledge are really high, but potentially could be reviewed after and assessed for that. 

I am curious how far can a system like this go. I do acknowledge that using AI as your main decision maker isn't great, still I feel I am far from the frontier of what it can achieve. 

Has anyone done a similar thing before?

replies.author: Ok-Draft2744
replies.body: Fair enough. How effective do you find it?

comments.author: Traditional_Ear5237
comments.body: if your system is based on LLMs - better don't, you will test many scenarios and will just burn a lot of money. With quant/stats models it makes sense to back test as they are rule based. When you have an LLM you can't reliably do that due to the model inherent bias, large cost per invoke (considering your thing is actually sophisticated), and temperature variation. And setting temperature at zero also does not make sense, yes it will be more deterministic but then you are losing a lot of intelligence from that. So unless you are running a 10 cent model - better not. We spent too much money doing that only to realize that the traditional thinking of back testing these systems simply does not apply, that and minus 10k USD from my account.

comments.author: tradematesHQ
comments.body: Your instinct about overfitting is correct  -  that's the whole game. Daily snapshots with live-captured news is the right approach because historical sentiment data is garbage. But here's the trap: if you iterate on the prompt until it looks good on past data, you've just built a curve fitter. The Fable-managed improvement idea is even riskier  -  you're optimizing against a known outcome. Split your data into three periods: develop, validate, and never-touch. Only run the final prompt once on the holdout. If it doesn't work there, it doesn't work.
